name: Tuxináwa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct Panoan variety, minimally attested; no phonological description located.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for this language. Lists †Tuchiunawa (var. Tutxiuanaua) as Headwaters subgroup II.C.viii.e, 'resembles Yaminawa dialects' (p. 11); Table 8: 127 lexicon entries, Carvalho (1931); appendix: 'Carvalho (1931: 249-252) 127-word list collected in 1923', located at mouth of Progresso Creek, upper Envira R. Keeps a separate, data-less 'Tushinawa' (II.C.viii.a, a Kashinawa clan per Tastevin 1926).

sources.citation: Carvalho, João Braulino de. 1929. Breve noticia sobre os indigenas que habitam a fronteira do Brasil com o Perú. In: Relatorio apresentado ao Presidente da Republica dos Estados Unidos do Brasil pelo Ministro de Estado das Relações Exteriores, Anno de 1928, 4.º vol., Annexo especial n. 2, pp. 301-332. Rio de Janeiro: Imprensa Nacional. (Reprinted 1931 in Boletim do Museu Nacional 7(3): 225-256 = Glottolog ref 304592.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Vocabulario Tutxiunaua' (pp. 324-326 of this printing, PDF pp. 27-29) is a bare 127-item word list obtained from one woman at the mouth of Progresso Creek in 1923; the only phonetic remark is 'Tú (ú-sôa como u francez)'. Some entries carry Portuguese-style accent marks (Ipá, Iuá, Uá, Uchá, Chatá, Pachá, Vô-né, Pulô) but no rule or comment on accent is given; the brief orthographic notes on p. 309 concern Poianaua (Poyanawa) only.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page tuxi1238 (Hammarström et al.) and Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú record biblio:carvalho-1929-breve
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's only references are Fleck 2013, Oliveira 2023 and Ethnologue 28 (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). The Nimuendajú record confirms the 1929 printing contains 'vocabulários poianaua, tutxiunaua, curina e remo'.
